output.brief: The jump in DC-stage write-offs is most likely caused by the Phase 2 cut in night receiving staff, not by Haverlow. Night dock-to-chamber time rose from about 44 minutes to about 3 h 52 min. Night write-off rates rose from 0.6% to 2.9% for every supplier, while day-shift rates stayed flat. Haverlow's trailer data shows product at 2.4–3.5°C when the doors opened, and loads were emptied by about 23:00. Receipt was confirmed and probed around 03:00, after the pallets had sat on an unrefrigerated dock at 15–17°C. The 7°C readings therefore reflect dock warming, not supplier abuse. Chambers held temperature. Don't raise the chargeback or move volume. Restore the night team to six (or otherwise fix the delay), set a maximum dock-to-chamber time monitored from scan data, and probe at unload. Don't drop the probe. The customer credit rise is a separate, smaller issue. Corriebank's self-certification began at the same time, and some credits may be loose claims, but the evidence is thin. Pull a sample of Corriebank claims and trace them to lots before asking for changes. I'm fairly confident (about 85%) on the main finding.
